summary: Job queue notifications in Business Central 2024 release wave 2: an assisted setup for recipients, methods and failure thresholds, an in-product notification strip and role center tiles, and external notifications through business events and Power Automate. The external part is in preview.
overview:
The video covers how Business Central can notify users when critical background processes such as job queues stop or fail. Administrators use an assisted setup guide with three steps: choose recipients, choose notification methods (in-product or external), and set frequency thresholds.

Users see a notification strip in their role center and three extra job queue tiles for failed, in-progress and pending tasks. Admins can see other users' job queue tasks. External notifications use the job queue task failed business event with a Power Automate template, and the video also covers new job queue APIs. The external part is in preview because business events are still in preview.
key_points: The assisted setup guide has three steps: select notification recipients, choose notification methods (in-product or external), and set frequency thresholds.
Thresholds reduce notification fatigue, for example notifying only after 3-5 consecutive failures instead of every failure.
The in-product notification strip in the role center lets users show details, inspect failed tasks, restart jobs manually, and disable notifications in My Settings.
Three role center tiles show tasks failed, in progress, and pending or waiting. Color-coded indicators follow the admin's failed-task thresholds.
Designated job queue notification administrators see their own job queue tasks and those of other users.
External notifications use the job queue task failed business event and a Power Automate template that can email through Outlook. This part is in preview because business events are in preview.
New APIs for job queue entries (with a restart bound action) and job queue log entries can be used from Power Automate flows.
